The exclusions in Section 8.2 are limited to use outside the Documentation and third-party modification — narrower than the customary carve-outs, with no combination exclusion. Critically, Section 9 excepts "LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8" from both the 12-month fee cap and the consequential-damages waiver, so the indemnity is uncapped rather than merely subject to a 3x super-cap. There is no reciprocal Corio indemnity anywhere in the Agreement (searches for "indemnif", "hold harmless" and "defend" return only Section 8), so nothing needs narrowing on our side. This exceeds the fallback and substantially meets the preferred position. Noted but not flagged as deviations: the indemnity does not add express limbs for Vendor's breach of applicable law, unauthorised access to Customer Data, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and affiliates are not separately named. These are sub-elements short of the preferred wording and do not warrant a redline given the indemnity is uncapped and one-way in our favour.

Rationale documents a reasonable search across the plausible homes for MFN/best-pricing language (Section 4 Fees, Exhibit B pricing/payment, Exhibit D cooperation) and the search terms used, supporting the preferred-position conclusion. Consistent with the claimed compliant status, no redline and no counterparty comment were proposed, and the rendered text is unchanged — appropriate treatment as internal evidence rather than a negotiation issue. No deterministic check failures; no indication of a Vendor-granted MFN in Customer's favour being incorrectly flagged or deleted.

quote: A. No Application Management Revenue shall be due for any Corio Customer subscriptions utilizing the initial 3000 Software User licenses granted herein, subject to a minimum limitation of 40 Authorized Software Users per Customer
rationale: The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, volume quota or take-or-pay obligation on Corio, so it meets the preferred position that fees are payable only for usage or ordered services. Exhibit B charges Corio a license fee, an annual MarketSite.net access fee and an annual maintenance fee for services actually received, plus a revenue share calculated as a percentage of Application Management Revenue Corio actually invoices (p0157), and implementation fees on a time-and-materials basis capped by the Statement of Work (p0161) - all consumption- or order-based rather than guaranteed spend. The only "minimum" (p0158) is a 40-user threshold that conditions a revenue-share waiver in Corio's favour; it does not obligate Corio to buy anything and is therefore not a commitment we would resist. Likewise the sole "shortfall" reference (p0059) is a reciprocal audit true-up - "the appropriate party shall promptly pay the amount of such shortfall or refund such overpayment" - which is precisely the true-up mechanic the playbook prefers over a penalty, and it runs both ways. Exhibit D's sales and marketing items are expressly "non-binding," and the initial-customers item (p0205) is only a commercially reasonable efforts undertaking, not a purchase or volume commitment. Two points noted but not flagged: maintenance is structured so that continuation is conditioned on Corio electing to keep paying ("provided that Corio continues to pay the annual Maintenance and Support fees," p0055), which preserves a practical exit rather than locking in five years of fees; and the five-year initial term has no termination-for-convenience right, but that is a term/termination issue outside this rule and would duplicate another rule's commercial term.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

The two 'minimum'/'shortfall' hits are correctly read as non-adverse: the 40-user threshold conditions a revenue-share waiver in Corio's favour, and the p0059 shortfall language is a reciprocal audit true-up, i.e. the mechanic the playbook prefers over a penalty. Sub-elements short of preferred (annual maintenance fees over a five-year term with no convenience termination, and the p0205 commercially reasonable efforts to obtain two customer orders) are appropriately noted in the rationale rather than flagged, and the term/termination point is correctly deferred to avoid double-flagging. No deterministic check failures; no over-flagging or directional error.

quote: Thereafter, this Agreement shall automatically renew for subsequent one (1) year periods unless either party provides the other party with written notification at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the initial five (5) year term or any one (1) year renewal thereof of its intention to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: Section 11.1 provides automatic renewals of one (1) year each — not multi-year — and either party (including us) may opt out on just thirty (30) days' written notice before the end of the initial term or any renewal term. That is a 30-day non-renewal window and a 12-month renewal term, which meets the preferred position (and is well inside the ≤60-day fallback and far from the >90-day walk-away). Exhibit pricing states MarketSite.net and maintenance/support fees for "Year 1" and "Year 2-5, and beyond," and the document contains no renewal-period uplift or repricing mechanic, so there is no uncapped escalator to cap. proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 11.3 preserves our license and Commerce One's post-termination support, but it lets Commerce One destroy our and our Customers' data with no return obligation, format or timeline. We have added a 30-day return of that data in a machine-readable format, followed by deletion and written certification, plus transition assistance at then-current rates; we can accept a 90-day assistance period if that is easier.

ops.text: 11.4 Transition Assistance and Data Return. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Commerce One shall (a) at Corio's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Commerce One's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Corio's request, return to Corio all data of Corio and its Customers and Software Users in Commerce One's possession or control in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion to Corio in writing, except to the extent retention is required by applicable law.

proposal.summary: Insert a data-return, deletion-certification and transition-assistance provision in Section 11

quote: Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, each party shall otherwise return or destroy any Confidential Information of the other party provided, however, Corio may retain any Confidential Information necessary for Corio to continue supporting it's then-existing Customers.
rationale: Transition continuity is well covered and in fact exceeds the preferred position: Section 11.3 and Section 5.3 make our license to serve then-existing Customers and Commerce One's support and maintenance obligations survive termination indefinitely (subject to fee payment), and Section 12 adds a source code escrow. However, the exit provisions contain no data return: Section 11.3 only requires each party to "return or destroy" the other's Confidential Information at Commerce One's election, with no obligation to return data of Corio, its Customers or Software Users held on the MarketSite.net Service, no machine-readable format, no 30-day deadline and no deletion certification. Because the fallback requires a data export within 30 days and the current wording permits outright destruction of our data (walk-away territory), this fails the fallback on a material term. We propose a narrow insert (new Section 11.4) requiring return within 30 days in a machine-readable format, then deletion with written certification, together with the preferred six-month transition assistance at then-current rates; the assistance period can drop to 90 days as a fallback.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

verification.notes: The rule targets post-termination data return and transition assistance; the cited exit provisions (Sections 11.3 and 5.3) contain only a 'return or destroy' obligation for Confidential Information at the other party's election, with no obligation to return Corio's or its Customers' hosted data, no machine-readable format, no 30-day deadline and no deletion certification — so the clause fails the fallback ('data export within 30 days') on a material term, making the deviation/insert classification correct rather than over-flagging. The redline is a pure insert (new Section 11.4) appended to the termination-effects section, leaving all existing language untouched — the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position, and it tracks the model language with party names correctly mapped (Commerce One as Vendor, Corio as Customer). The added legal-retention carve-out and 'at Corio's request' triggers are reasonable, do not weaken our position, and keep the deletion obligation from colliding with Commerce One's surviving post-termination support obligations to then-existing Software Users. The comment is accurate on what Section 11.3 does and does not do, states what changed and why, cites the playbook position and offers the 90-day fallback; tone, prefix and first-person plural are compliant. Deterministic checks confirm the operation applies and that data return/transition language is present in the result.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended the Warranty Period to twelve (12) months running from acceptance rather than sixty (60) days from the Effective Date with a fixed December 31, 1999 cut-off, since a period that can expire before or shortly after acceptance testing leaves us without a conformance warranty. Our playbook position is 12 months for software; we can accept ninety (90) days from acceptance as a fallback, and the existing correct/replace/refund remedy is unchanged.

quote: Commerce One warrants that the Software and MarketSite.net Service will perform in substantial accordance with the Documentation, and the media on which the Software is distributed will be free from defects in materials and workmanship under normal use, for a period of sixty (60) days from the Effective Date, but in no event not later than December 31, 1999 (the "Warranty Period").
rationale: Section 7.3 does contain a real express conformance warranty (Documentation conformance, media, no malicious code) and Section 7.3/7.4 plus the remedy paragraph give correction, replacement and, where breach cannot be corrected, termination with a refund of prepaid fees — so the remedy limb meets the playbook and the disclaimer (p0084) does not swallow the express warranties. The failure is duration: the Warranty Period is only sixty (60) days from the Effective Date and is hard-capped at December 31, 1999, whereas Acceptance Testing under Section 3.1 may itself run to December 31, 1999. The warranty can therefore expire on or before acceptance, falling below the fallback of ninety (90) days for software. We propose extending the period to twelve (12) months from acceptance (preferred), flagging ninety (90) days from acceptance as an acceptable fallback; the remedy and exclusions are left untouched.
